items.title: Dick Hyman interviewed by Monk Rowe, Clearwater Beach, Florida, March 17, 2001 [interview 2 of 2]
items.q: And that was with Butch and Milt and Bucky... We made two takes and they were both so good that we used the first one to open the album and the last one to close it.

ctx.x: It’s so perfect to me. It’s so perfect that if I had to play something, here’s an example of it.

Speaking about Milt though, unfortunately he was a little bit under-recorded on that album. It was done by a company which prides itself on doing things in natural sound without enhancing anything later on or even at the time, and Milt was not, I doubt if he was playing with an amplifier. I’ve always felt that unless you compensate a little bit as you play the record, he’s just a little bit under. But at any rate, yes, and the way that happened was that I asked Butch to get us going with a nice Count Basie tempo.
There you go. © Fillius Jazz Archive -15-
